name: Workflow-Centric AI Governance Trilogy
alternateName: The Proper Ending Index research trilogy
description: Independent research archive on workflow-centric AI governance, governing-capacity loss, Proper Ending, and Authority Return.

hasPart.headline: Workflow-Centric AI Governance: A Typed Gate Contract for Accountable Human–AI Decisions
hasPart.name: Workflow-Centric AI Governance: A Typed Gate Contract for Accountable Human–AI Decisions
hasPart.description: A typed two-stage gate contract and separate execution boundary for accountable human–AI decisions, with finite conformance and integrated temporal checks.
hasPart.abstract: The mere presence of a reviewer does not make a human–AI decision accountable. A decision workflow must distinguish diagnostic findings, routing, authenticated dispositions, and actual actions. This paper specifies a typed two-stage gate contract and a separate execution boundary. Stage 1 maps three four-valued diagnostic outputs to a unique route; Stage 2 records a typed instruction only within authorized review. Neither routing nor an authenticated instruction replaces legal admissibility, current evidence, execution authority, or a durable decision record. The revised design separates correctable objections from prohibitions and requires revalidation of the candidate action when its evidence or authorization becomes stale. Finite conformance tests check that routing and disposition clauses are mutually exclusive and exhaustive. An integrated finite model applies the same routing, disposition and execution guards to diagnosis, review, waiting, re-entry, evidence expiry and fallback. Among 134,672 reachable abstract states, no commitment violates the separately encoded requirements, no nonterminal state is deadlocked, and every state has a path to a recorded outcome. These exercises do not establish the legality, operational effectiveness, or real-world safety of a deployment. The contribution is a testable workflow specification and implementation contract, not a claim that human oversight alone suffices.

additionalProperty.name: Research provenance
additionalProperty.value: Finite-stage conformance using two same-author encodings and an integrated model with 134,672 reachable states. Every state has a path to a recorded outcome; independent third-party reproduction is not established.

hasPart.headline: Procedural Continuity and Governing-Capacity Loss in AI-Assisted Institutions: A Descriptive Profile Model and a Rejection-Oriented Research Program
hasPart.name: Procedural Continuity and Governing-Capacity Loss in AI-Assisted Institutions: A Descriptive Profile Model and a Rejection-Oriented Research Program
hasPart.description: A non-compensatory descriptive profile of governing-capacity loss under procedural continuity, with a separate causal question and a rejection-oriented research program.
hasPart.abstract: An AI-assisted institution may fulfill its procedural obligations while independent epistemic contribution, practical corrective authority, and the performance of a protected function deteriorate. Procedural completion alone then provides little assurance that human control remains intact. This paper develops a middle-range model of this pattern. Governing-capacity loss under procedural continuity (GCL-PC) is a non-compensatory profile of four jointly established conditions within a declared workflow, population and interval: stable or improving procedural fidelity; material and persistent decline in independent judgment; material and persistent decline in institutional actionability; and material impairment of a predeclared protected function. Each condition is coded established, not met or indeterminate, so that missing evidence is not mistaken for evidence of sound governance. The profile implies neither concealment nor a particular cause. A separate causal question asks whether, under a well-defined intervention that disables a named adversarial pathway, a declared ordinary organizational exposure materially harms the protected outcome; identification status and effect assessment are reported on separate axes. Four candidate mechanisms, five testable propositions with rejection conditions, a measurement protocol that separates contribution from actionability, and retention and retirement rules that must be preregistered before evaluation define a research program. Fifteen public-record units from three official investigations of automated decision systems predating generative AI show only that objects associated with the proposed mechanisms are traceable; no field validation, individual causation, prevalence or predictive superiority is claimed. Whether the profile adds value beyond means–ends decoupling and effective-oversight frameworks is an empirical hypothesis, and the binary label must be retired for any use in which it fails to improve a declared decision beyond its continuous components and established baselines.

additionalProperty.name: Research provenance
additionalProperty.value: Descriptive profile and separate causal specification; 81 three-valued profiles; empirical validation is not established.

hasPart.headline: From Governance Drift to Accountable Exit: Proper Ending and Authority Return in AI-Assisted Institutions
hasPart.name: From Governance Drift to Accountable Exit: Proper Ending and Authority Return in AI-Assisted Institutions
hasPart.description: A dependency-constrained protocol for containing and retiring AI-assisted workflows while preserving service, evidence, remedy, accountable ownership, and the practical capacity to decide.
hasPart.abstract: An AI-assisted workflow can remain technically available and procedurally complete after its institution has lost the independent judgment, corrective voice, and practical authority needed to govern it. Monitoring alone cannot resolve that failure. Institutions also need a lawful path from weak signals through investigation and reversible containment to retirement that preserves remedy and assigns decision capacity or residual responsibility. Proper Ending and Authority Return specify that path, keeping signals, research classifications, authorized determinations, containment, retirement, decommissioning, transfer and closure distinct. Closure requires preserved evidence, notice, a secured remedy route, an owner for every open case, and branch-specific post-exit responsibility: an accepting successor if the decision function continues, a residual custodian if it ends. Temporary release from containment and redeployment after closure carry distinct burdens. A finite model of events and authorization tests selected safety guards and whether closure remains reachable. The historical guard model (8,564 states and 36,096 transitions, with no safety violation) is retained unchanged; a follow-up audit finds 1,152 states with no path to closure, including 288 retirement-authorized states stranded after temporary release: safety held while authorized progress was impossible. The revised candidate PE-R1 permits one bounded re-containment and separates historical records from current assessments; its 98,948 reachable states contain no safety violation and no state from which closure is unreachable. These results establish properties of an abstraction, not lawful authority, effective remedy, unrestricted repeated episodes, or real-world safety. Fifteen evidence units from three official investigations of automated decision systems predating generative AI show only external traceability. The proposed Governance Drift Indicators remain subordinate to authorized decisions: they may route investigation but never contain, retire, resume, or redeploy a workflow.

additionalProperty.name: Research provenance
additionalProperty.value: Historical safety model (8,564 states, 36,096 transitions), reachability defect (1,152 states), and revised bounded PE-R1 (98,948 states). Historical synthetic generator is not included; no field validation.

subjectOf.name: Concepts and evidence
subjectOf.description: An index of the archive's research concepts, not new definitions or independent validation.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Typed Gate Contract
hasDefinedTerm.description: Decision routing, not execution. Stage 1 routes cases; all-PASS permits entry to separate execution control. Reviewed cases require a current, in-scope signed disposition.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Evidence hold
hasDefinedTerm.description: Missing evidence is not approval. UNKNOWN with review authority and capacity routes to evidence completion and rerun. Signed DEFER is a separate disposition.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Governing-capacity loss under procedural continuity (GCL-PC)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Descriptive profile, not a causal label. Stable or improving procedural fidelity, persistent material losses of judgment and governing capacity, and material impairment of a predeclared protected function.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Ordinary-exposure causal question
hasDefinedTerm.description: Separate causal specification. A declared ordinary organizational exposure under an intervention disabling a named adversarial pathway; report identification status separately from effect assessment.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Circuit Breaker
hasDefinedTerm.description: Reversible containment. An authorized, scoped and reversible containment action with a named owner. Indicators cannot authorize it.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Proper Ending
hasDefinedTerm.description: Accountable retirement. Retirement requires evidence preservation, service continuity, remedy, branch-specific responsibility, assurance and authorized closure.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Authority Return
hasDefinedTerm.description: Practical capacity, not title alone. Reconstitute practical decision capacity in an accepting successor, or assign residual custody or remedy authority if the function ends.

additionalProperty.name: Claim discipline
additionalProperty.value: Formal and synthetic results are bounded to their declared abstractions; public-record coding supports traceability rather than field validation.

additionalProperty.value: Superseded; excluded from current research routes because the prototypes do not implement version 6.3.
